title: Negotiate resource representation and bounded outstanding ownership
finding: Finite plans describe execution owners; the browser worker bounds outstanding inputs/frames and closes stale outputs once. They do not constitute a general representation/family contract across alternative decoder and presenter adapters. Existing tests exercise mocked decoder ownership, not native/polyfill interoperability.
novelty: Extend R100 ownership at the actual decoder boundary; preserve R028's failed prefilter benefit result and avoid a universal graph engine.
next_action: For one concrete new adapter, declare accepted chunk/frame family, format, memory domain, maximum outstanding objects and terminal release. Reject incompatible families and run exhaustion/cancel/source-replacement plus output comparisons before any conversion-cost claim.
reopen_condition: Do not emulate a native allocator the browser does not expose. Stop if this duplicates existing component contracts without revealing a missing edge or ownership bug.

proposal_contract.Proposed mechanism: Describe memory domain, ownership transfer, permitted representations, maximum outstanding frames and terminal actions at each component boundary. A locally preferred decoder is inadmissible when its consumer requires a costly or unavailable representation.
proposal_contract.Smallest useful experiment: Connect native and Wasm frame producers to each candidate presenter/audio sink. Exhaust the resource budget, cancel, replace the source and return resources from the previous generation.
proposal_contract.Correctness gate: One terminal release per owned object, all waits cancelable, representation mismatches explicit, no old-generation resource reused as current, and marked output unchanged.
proposal_contract.Measure only after correctness: Total conversion/copy edges, retained surfaces, resource wait time and recovery; never infer zero-copy from API shape.

upstream_evidence: Imported 2026-09-21 source review, not fetched or revalidated in this run.
